original_card.question: Does a new paid-profile or mixture-ceiling claim have independent source-bound coverage of its actual changed ledger?
methods: Independently reconstruct one changed paid ledger or pooled dual with exact source and model binding.
Check a genuinely uncovered moment implication with a different enclosure method and semantic controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls. Name the existing checks and the missing coverage. More digits or another equivalent evaluation of an unchanged root is not by itself new verification coverage.

first_step.inspect: Choose one uncovered implication in #4088 literal mixed fill, #4091 pooled dual/model binding or #4067 changed frame/host bill. #4091 pins an earlier #4088 head: validate word, capacity and stock equivalence before applying that ceiling to the later fill.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Independently reconstruct one changed ledger or pooled certificate with a positive case and a semantic failure control. Compare exact sources and name what existing checks miss. Keep this separate from supplier-boundary-audit (ordinary/outer dispatch) and uniform-transfer-audit (all-size proof). Stop after the chosen implication; more digits of an unchanged root are not additional mechanism coverage.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.

actual_scope: Certify per-cut divisibility and unchanged normalized leaf cost of PR #4507's chronological batching for PR #4483's arbitrary-height forests (batch-level transfer), with an independent literal ordered-word/paid-path oracle, closed-form cut formulas, authenticated source Flow comparison, semantic rejection controls, and a conditional all-rank uniform width envelope (WIDTH.md).
scope_change_reason: Take #4507 open question 2 after live overlap review instead of the catalogue card's independent-moment audit. The result is a batching transfer and finite accounting; #4483 already covers arbitrary-height aggregate flow, #4519 independently recomputes #4507's original widths and #4521 counts the expanded compiler, so none of that is claimed here.
bottleneck_link: A constructive finite compiler at adaptive heights needs every suspended chronological cut to be a whole number of supplier invocations; aggregate histograms hide infeasible cuts. Side result: no exponent, kappa or native admission changes.
stop_rule: One transfer theorem with its proof, one literal-oracle replay over bounded toy flows, toy and pinned-p7 least-width compilations, semantic controls, and the conditional width envelope with pinned p7/native4453/p16 geometry probes; stop before native admission, convergence claims or a tighter all-rank valuation analysis.
evidence: Direct isolated verify.py passed: 405 census fixtures, 19089 literal oracle classes, 2304 brute-force minimality cases, 186476 chronological constraints in six compilations and 25 controls. Final width_bound.py passed four finite compilations with 13377 constraints, three pinned profile applications and two controls, including a zero-visit level. RESULT.json and WIDTH-RESULT.json preserve exact receipts; WIDTH.md gives the symbolic all-rank proof. Separate different-family reviews and optimized replays passed for both implementations. No human or proof-kernel acceptance.
author: codyw912, with substantial OpenAI assistance; builds on Mihir Srivastava's #4507, zxv's #4436/#4483 and Jacob Alan Sussman's integer compiler
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance in code, proofs and writing: Anthropic implementation of the cut compiler, OpenAI implementation of the width witnesses and coordination, independent Anthropic mathematical challenge supplying the level-run proof, OpenAI cut-compiler review/replay and Anthropic width-proof/implementation review/replay. No human or proof-kernel verification is claimed.

open_questions.question: Do the retuned geometries (for example PR #4533 height base 768 for p16) keep the same per-cut divisibility and width envelope?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The application probes bind only the BENCHMARKS height bases; a retuned M changes the forest and its cut inventory.
open_questions.first_step: Add the retuned (M, g) rows to the geometry probes of width_bound.py with an authenticated profile pin and compare each cap against the source Flow.
open_questions.blocked_by: A pinned retuned profile and its authenticated source bytes.

open_questions.question: Can the all-rank width envelope be tightened with actual gcd savings or narrower semigroup counts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: WIDTH.md bounds log B_N only from above and cannot compare against any nested-width lower bound.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the exact prime-valuation recurrence at selected pinned p7 ranks, then derive a symbolic inequality retaining gcd cancellation; finite fits alone are not an asymptotic proof.
open_questions.blocked_by: Cost of exact large-rank compilation; an eventual source-count lower bound is needed for any exponential-versus-subexponential comparison.
